GPT-6.2

We’re introducingGPT‑6.2 Astra, our new frontier model for your hardest projects, andGPT‑6.2 Sol, our efficient, versatile model for everyday work. Both models deliver better results on demanding tasks with fewer output tokens, so you can get more done within your usage limits. For businesses and developers, that means frontier performance at costs that make sense at scale.

GPT‑6.2 Astra sets a new quality bar for AI in complex professional work. Its slides, spreadsheets, and documents read less like AI, and more closely follow the templates you provide and the conventions of your field. It writes cleaner code and builds frontends that look and work better, particularly for websites, gaming, and 3D design.

On Agents’ Last Exam, which tests multistep professional work, GPT‑6.2 Astra sets a new high, scoring 5.2 points higher than GPT‑6 Astra at less than a third of the cost, and 5.5 points ahead of Claude Fable 5.2 at just 5% of the cost.

Agents’ Last Exam evaluates models on long-horizon professional workflows. Its leaderboard results for Fable 5.2 exclude nine tasks that used a fallback model.

We believe GPT-6.2 Astra is the best model in the world for scientists. It sets a new high on Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, which tests how well models can carry out scientific work in a terminal. GPT-6.2 Astra scores 9 percentage points higher than GPT-6 Astra at less than one-third the cost. It also sets a new high on the Vals Science Index, which asks models to interpret real biological data and run experiments to infer how a simulated system works.

In the API, GPT‑6.2 Astra’s input and output token prices are 20% lower than GPT‑6 Astra’s, with a 60% discount on cached input ($8 for input, $0.40 for cached input, and $40 for output, all per million tokens). GPT‑6.2 Sol keeps GPT‑6.1 Sol’s API token prices. On several benchmarks, both models come close to or outperform other leading models at a small fraction of the cost per task.

Compared with GPT‑6.1 Sol, GPT‑6.2 Sol is smarter, more efficient, and lets you complete more tasks on the same paid plan. It powers through multistep agentic workflows, writes clearly and naturally, and is intuitive to collaborate with. Many employees at OpenAI use it as their default model for both technical and non-technical tasks.

In Cognition’s FrontierCode 2.0, GPT‑6.2 Sol comes within 0.5 points of GPT‑6.2 Astra at about one-fifth the cost (both at max).

FrontierCode 2.0 evaluates whether changes to real codebases meet maintainers’ standards for merging.

Its speed and intelligence also make it ideal for the important tasks people turn to AI for outside of work. On our recently releasedLifeVal⁠evaluation, which measures performance on challenging everyday tasks, GPT‑6.2 Sol outscores GPT‑6 Astra at about one-seventh the cost.

LifeVal tests how well models handle everyday tasks tailored to someone’s needs, such as shortlisting kindergartens after a move, finding a home that fits a family’s budget and commute, or planning meals for a parent adjusting to a new diagnosis.

We trained GPT‑6.2 Astra to create clearer, better-designed slides, spreadsheets, and documents that more closely follow the conventions professionals use in fields like law, sales, finance, and accounting. The writing is more direct and specific, with fewer generic takeaways and less filler.

Harvey LAB‑AA v1.1 uses legal assignments to test whether models can find the relevant facts across source documents, apply them to a detailed brief, and produce an accurate deliverable that meets every requirement. GPT‑6.2 Astra sets a new state of the art, more than doubling Claude Fable 5.2’s pass rate at about one-sixth the cost.Astra for Law⁠, our configuration of GPT-6.2 Astra for lawyers, scores even higher on this benchmark.

Harvey LAB‑AA tests legal work such as reviewing contract provisions. Its headline score gives credit only when a deliverable meets every grading criterion and contains no material hallucinations.

Our internal GDPval v2 benchmark is our next iteration ofGDPval⁠that measures complex, long-horizon workflows from real projects in sectors like consulting, finance, and design. GPT‑6.2 Astra leads the models we tested, up 6.2 percentage points from GPT‑6 Astra while using 22% fewer output tokens. GPT‑6.2 Sol improves 5.3 points from GPT‑6.1 Sol.

GDPval v2 consists of long-horizon knowledge-work assignments from real projects in sectors like finance, data science, biotechnology, and marketing.

Building a valuation workbook or writing an investment memo starts with finding the relevant figures in source files and working out how they fit together. Artificial Analysis’s AA‑AnalystAgent tests that work on real spreadsheets and reports. In one task, models use California Medicaid’s expenditure reports to calculate how much the program spent on medical transport. GPT‑6.2 Astra sets a new high, answering 62.5% of questions correctly on all five independent attempts.

GPT‑6.2 Astra is our best model yet at designing slides and following slide templates, whether given an original file or even a screenshot. It can match the layout, colors, and typography down to the exact font size, and carry the template’s writing style into new slides. Early testers found the decks easier to use directly with fewer edits, thanks to titles that state the main takeaway and concise body copy that focuses on the details readers need.

We evaluated GPT-6.2 Astra on turning dense information into readable briefs and infographics for both technical and non-technical audiences. Examples included trading briefs and diagrams of agentic workflows.

GPT-6.2 Astra's documents were a significant step up from GPT-6 Astra. The writing and charts made it much easier to pick out the key points of a briefing, and the diagrams clarified complex systems by showing how the parts work together.

In our Agent evals, GPT-6.2 Astra used 62% fewer tokens than GPT-6.1 Sol on complex legal-agent tasks. Astra was strongest on legal research, scoring higher than alternative models on 8 of the 10 research tasks we tested, across tax, M&A and litigation work.

GPT-6.2 Astra is a notable step up from GPT-6 Astra, completing more than 3x as many Legal Agent Benchmark tasks in our evaluations with 34.5% fewer output tokens. For internal memos drafting tasks, GPT-6.2 Astra caught more weaknesses in the client’s position, and drafted filings made fewer unwarranted concessions.

On the apps, dashboards and slides ClickUp Brain builds inside the workspace, GPT-6.2 Astra edged out our production model in blind testing. What stood out was how it got there: about 40% fewer tokens and 30% fewer review rounds.

GPT‑6.2 Astra’s more precise computer use lets it work down to individual parts and connections in CAD and simulation tools. Engineers can use that additional detail to check how components fit, see where loads shift as a design moves, and test revisions before building a prototype.

We asked GPT‑6.2 Astra to visualize chassis dynamics of a car on a mountain road. Astra created the 3D model and wrote a Python solver to simulate complex dynamics between the tires and suspension, then animated the results in Blender. This enables engineers to quickly test new designs and improve simulation accuracy over time.

GPT‑6.2 Astra can model a mechanical system part by part, giving engineers a way to show how it goes together and test how design changes affect its behavior.

Our team used GPT‑6.2 Astra to turn the scalloped balconies of Chicago’s Marina City towers into a lamp. The video follows the design from reference photos through CAD revisions to a physical lamp assembled by hand. The site, generated by GPT-6.2 Astra, can be used to create your own paper lamp.

GPT‑6.2 Astra brings stronger visual reasoning to web design, choosing layouts and imagery that give each site a distinctive look and building elements around the actual goal of the site.

Those gains in visual reasoning and computer use carry over to 3D design. GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol can turn a written brief into an interactive browser experience, from a pinball table you can play to a recreation of the Colosseum you can explore from different angles. On Artificial Analysis’s AA‑3D, human judges try two blinded experiences built from the same prompt and vote for the one they prefer. GPT‑6.2 Astra ranks first with 1,318 Elo, followed by Claude Fable 5.2 at 1,271 and GPT‑6.2 Sol at 1,259.

GPT-6.2 Astra is a huge leap forward for creative work. It makes Higgsfield Miracle possible, powering real-time video editing with pixel-level precision and giving creators ultimate creative control. In our internal 3D generation evals, it achieved the target result in one shot in 73% of cases, while GPT-6 Astra needed three or more iterations. This saves our creative team a lot of time and allows for more efficient fully agentic workflows.

GPT‑6.2 Astra has better judgment about how to execute a task, including matching its tools and effort to the workflow, and knowing when to use plugins versus computer use.

On coding, GPT-6.2 Astra is better at implementing and testing complex changes in existing codebases. Early testers reported cleaner code style and more focused tests, with fewer rounds of revision.

GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol mark another significant jump in cyber capabilities. They find and exploit vulnerabilities more effectively, write more secure code, and produce better patches, with substantial token-efficiency gains on several evaluations. LikeGPT‑6 Astra⁠, 6.2 Astra and Sol meet the Critical threshold for cybersecurity under ourPreparedness Framework⁠.

Due to their increased capabilities, we’re launching GPT‑6.2 Astra and Sol with tighter safeguards for higher-risk cybersecurity assistance. These protections reduce misuse risk, but also restrict some legitimate vulnerability research and security testing workflows. Help every seller shorten the sales cycle, from finding the right accounts to following through on customer commitments, with a new Sales experience and over 30 new and expanded partner plugins.

We’re introducing ChatGPT for Sales to help every sales team understand customers better, spend less time on busywork, and close more deals. It includes our new Sales plugin with dedicated skills for sellers, and more than 30 new and enhanced partner plugins in ChatGPT, so you can use information from the tools your team already relies on to prepare for calls, tailor proposals, and follow up faster.

The new Sales plugin from OpenAI gives you ready-to-use workflows for everyday sales work, from deciding which accounts to pursue to preparing for a call and drafting the follow-up.Sales teams work best when everyone has a shared understanding of the customer.Which accounts are worth pursuing? What does a buyer need to move forward? Which deals need attention, and why? The answers often sit across teammates, prospecting tools, customer calls, and the CRM. Bringing that information together gives teams more time to make informed decisions and follow through on customer commitments. That starts with the work you do every day.

ChatGPT for Sales brings your tools, customer context, and sales workflows into one place. It also gives your team access to partner plugins, so ChatGPT can use customer context from your existing tools to help move opportunities forward. Choose the partner plugins that fit your sales process.

Create content and equip sellers. Learn your sales process and the latest product updates with Confluence, Guru, and Seismic. Rehearse pitches and practice handling objections with ChatGPT Voice. Build tailored presentations with ChatGPT Slides, Gamma, Figma, or Canva, or create an interactive demo or ROI calculator with ChatGPT Sites.

Manage accounts and advance deals. Bring together account context from Salesforce, HubSpot, Close CRM, or monday CRM to prepare for calls, review customer commitments, and plan next steps.

Find and engage buyers. Combine account signals from Apollo, Clay, and Common Room with ChatGPT’s web research to understand what’s changing at an account and identify reasons to reach out. Use Outreach or Salesloft to plan your outreach.

Turn customer conversations into action. Use call notes from the Meetings plugin in ChatGPT, Gong, Otter.ai, or Granola to understand buyer priorities, capture agreed next steps, and draft follow-ups.

Track performance and spot deal risk. Use signals from Backstory to identify deals that need attention. Analyze connected sales data with the Data plugin in ChatGPT or Hex to explain what changed in the pipeline and where to focus next.

Prepare quotes and agreements. Bring in Docusign, Ironclad, PandaDoc, or ServiceNow CPQ to help prepare quotes and agreements when a buyer is ready to move forward.

You can also keep work moving between conversations by delegating to yourdot—an always-on agent in ChatGPT. Your dot can use these same plugins and customer context to prepare meeting briefs, track deal updates, and proactively bring you relevant changes and proposed next steps for review.

Use ChatGPT to build a prioritized account list from your CRM information and prospect research from tools like ZoomInfo and Clay. Ask why each account fits, identify missing information, and refine the list around your team’s priorities. Then turn that research into outreach with a specific reason to engage—all in the same conversation.

Before a meeting, ask for a briefing that brings together account history, previous calls, and the buyer’s priorities. Explore what still needs an answer, then turn that preparation into a customer-specific pitch with Gamma or Canva. Refine the story in the conversation before your meeting.

After a call, have ChatGPT draft the follow-up, capture agreed next steps, and prepare updates to the customer record. Refine the message in the conversation and review the proposed changes. With connected tools like Attio, you can save the next step to your CRM from ChatGPT.

Ask ChatGPT to help you understand what is holding up a deal, using CRM history and customer conversations. With Rox, you can also ask a dot to check the deal each morning, flag changes that need attention, and prepare a meeting brief or follow-up sequence for your review.

See a few examples from across the sales ecosystem showing how these tools work in ChatGPT:

From account research to deal follow-through, hear how sales teams are putting ChatGPT for Sales to work.

Install the Sales plugin⁠(opens in a new window)to get started, andlearn more about ChatGPT for Salesand the partner plugins. Availability of partner plugins and features varies by plan, region, and workspace settings.

ChatGPT Business and Enterprise admins can enable ChatGPT for Sales for your team by opening theAdmin Console⁠(opens in a new window),selecting your workspace, and selecting Plugins. Make the Sales plugin and relevant partner plugins available for members to install, orinstall them⁠(opens in a new window)by default for your team. Review access to the required apps and the actions they can use. Workspace members can complete any required account connections when prompted.

We’re continuing to build ChatGPT for Sales and the partner plugin ecosystem around the work sales teams do every day. Our goal is to bring more of that work into ChatGPT, with connected tools and customer context that carries from finding an opportunity to preparing for a conversation and following through.

Our latest model configuration earned leading marks on multiple benchmarks. Every ChatGPT Enterprise customer can now request access.

Today, we're releasing an updated Astra for Law that is state-of-the-art on Harvey LAB-AA and a top performer on Vals AI’s Legal Research Bench. We are also enabling all ChatGPT Enterprise customers to request access through the Trusted Access Program, including through the API.

Astra for Law is a model configuration ofGPT‑6.2 Astra⁠, our latest, most powerful frontier model. It pairs GPT‑6.2 Astra with an expanded legal search index and instructions for researching a question, weighing the authorities, and writing the answer. Today’s configuration earned full credit on the LAB-AA tests nearly 40% more often than did the runner-up, GPT‑6.2 Astra.

Since weintroduced Astra for Law in September⁠to a small group of firms, includingCooley⁠,Ropes & Gray⁠, andSullivan & Cromwell⁠, our research team has made rapid innovations to improve its legal reasoning and expand its legal search index by over a third. OnVals AI’s Legal Research Bench⁠(opens in a new window), the share of research answers that passed every check rose from about 46% to 53.8% in less than two months.

As the world grows more complex, lawyers occupy an increasingly important role. They shape nearly every system we rely on: they negotiate the agreements that move commerce, defend people’s rights in courts, and draft the laws we all live by. That’s why we’ve made law a research priority at OpenAI: to put the best intelligence in the hands of the best lawyers.

Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB) tests whether a model can take a legal assignment from start to finish.LAB-AA⁠(opens in a new window)is Artificial Analysis’s version of that test. It tests the models on 120 assignments developed by Harvey across 24 areas of law – everything from drafting deposition outlines to reviewing commercial leases to strategizing ownership changes in acquisitions. To earn full credit, an answer must meet every requirement of an assignment without hallucinating, i.e., making a material claim that is not supported by the source documents.

Astra for Law ranked first, earning full credit on 20.8% of assignments, ahead of GPT‑6.2 Astra at 15.0% and Muse Wonder Full at 13.1%.

Astra for Law ranked first at 20.8%, earning full credit about59% more often than Muse Wonder Full, the highest-scoring non-OpenAI model.

Astra for Law also earned that top score with54% less output per assignmentthan the highest-scoring non-OpenAI model in the evaluation, averaging about 64,000 output tokens per assignment, compared with 139,000 for Muse Wonder Full. For legal teams paying by usage, this can mean the difference between staying within budget and blowing through it.

Each dot is a model configuration. Higher means more assignments earned full credit; farther left means fewer output tokens, which include the text a model generates as it reasons and writes. Astra for Law averaged about 64,000 output tokens per assignment and earned full credit on 20.8%, compared with 139,000 and 13.1% for Muse Wonder Full. No configuration shown matched Astra for Law’s score using fewer output tokens.

Hallucinations are unacceptable in legal work. A single invented citation can cost a lawyer a client’s trust, credibility in court, and a reputation built over years. That’s why reducing hallucinations has been a priority for Astra for Law. In Artificial Analysis’s latest LAB-AA comparison, Astra for Law tied (with GPT‑6) for thelowest rate of material hallucinations:0.03 per assignment, compared with 0.59 for Claude Opus 5.5 (the next lowest non-OpenAI model). Notably, Astra for Law's performance on this eval includedzero material hallucinations for tasks that met the all-pass criteria.

Astra for Law averaged 0.03 material and 0.06 minor hallucinations per assignment. Claude Opus 5.5 averaged 0.59 material and 0.51 minor hallucinations per assignment, about 20 times as many material hallucinations and 8.5 times as many minor ones.

Across the same 120 assignments, Artificial Analysis counted hallucinated claims that could mislead a reader on a substantive point. Astra for Law averaged 0.03 such errors per assignment, tied for the lowest rate in the comparison and roughly half the rate for regular GPT‑6.2 Astra (0.06).

Every OpenAI configuration tested had fewer hallucinations than Claude Opus 5.5, the best non-OpenAI result on this measure. Opus 5.5 averaged 0.59 material hallucinations per assignment, about 20 times as many as Astra for Law.

We've made law a research priority at OpenAI, dedicating a team of researchers to accelerate innovation for frontier legal intelligence. One early measure of their progress comes fromVals AI’s Legal Research Bench⁠(opens in a new window), where practicing lawyers set questions about U.S. federal and state law. An answer has to cover every required point and pass the source checks. In September, Astra for Law earned full credit on about 46% of questions. In Vals AI’s November 16 evaluation, it earned full credit on 112 of 208 questions (53.8%),a gain of about eight percentage points in under two months. Across all questions, it earned90.9% of the available points, including partial credit.

In less than two months, the share of legal research questions on which Astra for Law earned full credit rose from about 46% to 53.8%, a gain of about eight percentage points.

Astra for Law (green) sits in the small cluster of top performers on Vals AI’s Legal Research Bench.

Building Astra for Law as a model configuration lets us stay on the bleeding edge of the frontier, in this caseGPT‑6.2 Astra⁠. On top of this foundation, we iteratively refine Astra for Law’s specific settings and instructions in response to practitioner feedback, teaching it how to reason and write like a seasoned lawyer. We also continuously hone its tools, such as the legal search index. Since September, we’ve grown the index by 34%, adding over 80 million new URLs, including across international jurisdictions such as theUK, Australia, and Canada. Today, the updated index spans over 310 million URLs and coversmore than 99.9% of published U.S. precedential case law⁠(opens in a new window).

The chart below shows how the model configuration takes advantage of both the speed of frontier innovation and builds on top of that the specific requirements that make it powerful for lawyers. On Harvey’s own Legal Agent Benchmark, GPT‑6 Astra met every requirement on4.6%of assignments. GPT‑6.2 Astratripled performance,completing14.6%under the same conditions. With the legal configuration, that rose to16.2%, completing 11% more questions than GPT‑6.2 Astra.

This chart shows both the rate of development in frontier intelligence, as well as the impact of the model configuration. The full-credit rate more than tripled from GPT‑6 Astra to GPT‑6.2 Astra, then rose another 11% with the legal configuration. This test comes from Harvey’s own LAB (separate from the previously discussed LAB-AA).

The most interesting possibilities for Astra for Law are being shaped by the lawyers who are using it for their day-to-day work. Across law firm customers and OpenAI’s own legal team, early users are building references around their practice, inviting tougher challenges to their arguments, and finding new ways to respond to changing legislation.

For example, early users at OpenAI are using Astra for Law to:

Give your argument its strongest opponent.A common use for Astra for Law is as a sparring partner. A competition lawyer gives it a reading of a statute and asks it to argue the other side, drawing on legislative history, court decisions, and versions of the law in other languages.

Find the line between a recommendation and a requirement.A policy lawyer looking at a proposed oversight bill wanted to know how much power an independent reviewer would have. If the reviewer called for a fix, would the developer have to make it? For questions like these, the lawyer puts a plain-English account of each obligation beside the bill’s exact words, so she can make fast judgment calls about which reading the text supports.

Start the first call with outside counsel on the hardest question.When the business is considering entering an unfamiliar industry, a product lawyer uses Astra for Law to map which rules would apply to the proposed activity. Instead of spending the first call asking for high-level advice, the lawyer can bring outside counsel what’s actually at issue.

Turn a stack of policies into a workflow.A legal program manager used Astra for Law to turn regulatory procedures and company policy into a workflow for colleagues handling incoming cases, enabling them to automate when to ask for more information, when to close the case, and when to escalate it to a lawyer.

Build the guide you wish came with the statute.A competition lawyer paired Astra for Law with ChatGPT’s site-building tools to annotate legislation the team uses regularly. A colleague reading a provision can hover over a term for its definition, follow a link to the materials that explain it, and see what the team advised the last time that provision came up.

Starting today, every ChatGPT Enterprise customer can request Astra for Law through the Trusted Access Program in the admin console. If your team already has access, selectgpt-6.2-astra-lawin ChatGPT. Customers can also request API access to build Astra for Law into their own toolsusing this form⁠.

articles.title: Perplexity Computer Adds Multiagent: Up to 16 AI Agents That Cross-Check Work
articles.content: Perplexity has added Multiagent to Computer, its agent platform for research and multistep work. Perplexity Computer Multiagent is a new effort level that sits above Ultra. A lead agent runs a team of agents on different frontier models. Those agents work in parallel, share findings directly and check each other’s work. For developers and analysts, the change is structural. Supporting agents no longer report only to a single lead. TL;DR Size: Up to 16 agents per task, plus the lead. Context length: Not disclosed. Runs on: Perplexity’s cloud. Web only, Perplexity Max plan. No local or quantized option. Performance: Not benchmarked. Perplexity published no accuracy or speed numbers. Best: 16-agent cap with direct agent-to-agent checks across 3 default model families (Claude, GPT, Gemini). What is Perplexity Computer Multiagent? Multiagent is the highest effort level in Perplexity Computer. It coordinates AI models to analyze complex tasks and cross-check their work, per Perplexity’s announcement. It builds on effort controls launched on September 17, 2026. That release added 4 settings: Light, Standard, High and Ultra. Each setting picks the orchestrator model and its reasoning depth. Lower settings use less expensive models. How does Multiagent work? The lead agent plans the task and assigns parts to supporting agents. It can assign up to 16 agents and also does part of the work itself. In Perplexity’s example, Claude Fable 5.2 plans the task. It splits work among agents running Claude Opus 5.5, GPT 6.1 Sol and Gemini 4 Carbon. Those 3 models form the default team. Fable 5.2 and GPT 6 Astra join as supporting agents only when requested or needed. Key mechanics from the launch post: Direct sharing: Agents use evidence found by others, question assumptions and flag discrepancies. Shared files: Agents coordinate edits to shared files. One agent can update revenue assumptions and notify another to reuse them in a valuation. Single point of contact: Users talk only to the lead. The lead merges findings into one response. Follow-ups: The lead tells affected agents what changed. The team continues its existing work. Control: Users see which agents and models are running. Stopping the thread stops the whole team. Model choice: Users can name specific models in their query. Multiagent vs Ultra vs Model Council Perplexity now offers 3 ways to put several models on 1 problem: Ultra: One lead delegates to supporting agents. Those agents report only to the lead. Multiagent: The same lead model as Ultra coordinates agents. They talk to each other and edit shared deliverables. Model Council: Several models answer the same question independently. Computer then shows where they agree and disagree. Model Council came to Computer in July 2026. Perplexity positions Multiagent for large, interconnected work that can run in parallel. Its examples include deal data room diligence, multi-scenario forecasts, annual report review, competing-hypothesis research and year-end tax preparation. && How does it compare with other multi-agent products? articles.title: Liquid AI Releases d1.2 and d1.2-ultra: Omnimodal Decision Models That Top the AA Decision Index
articles.content: Liquid AI just released d1.2 and d1.2-ultra. A decision model does not write text. It returns calibrated probabilities over a fixed set of answers. The Liquid AI d1.2 decision model family now accepts text, images and audio. It also adds 5 new answer types. d1.2-ultra scores 75 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index v2.1, the top score among decision models on the index. You can check the deployment options and specs here through our GPULeaderboard.com chrome extension. TL;DR Size: Parameters not disclosed. Up to 65,536 input tokens per question, 128 questions per call. Runs on: Hosted Liquid API only. No weights yet; Liquid AI says it will open them “at some point”. Performance: d1.2-ultra 75 and d1.2 69 on the AA Decision Index v2.1. Best: 0.8-point calibration error for d1.2-ultra across 13 benchmarks (Liquid AI test). What is Liquid AI d1.2? d1.2 is a hosted decision model from Liquid AI that answers typed questions about text, images or audio in 1 call. It returns a probability per option and generates zero output tokens, so only input is billed. d1.2-ultra targets harder decisions. d1.2 is faster and costs less than half as much. The model IDs are d1.2 (default) and d1.2-ultra. Earlier d1, d1.1 and d1-ultra are now deprecated and do not support audio or the new tasks. What are the 5 new tasks in d1.2? d1.2 adds 5 typed answers on the same endpoint and request format: Read a value (text, number, date): returns the value plus the characters it came from. It answers “not found” instead of guessing. Find every span (spans): returns each matching passage, such as names or emails, with its position. Locate objects (box, boxes): returns 1 rectangle, or 1 per instance with a count. Estimate a number (number with range): returns a best guess and a range, for example 12 within 10 to 14. Pick every option that applies (choice with multiple): returns each matching label with its own probability. How does audio input work? Audio can be the subject of a question, such as which language is spoken or whether a siren is audible. The question can also be spoken. The API takes 16-bit PCM WAV and counts 10 tokens per second of audio. On held-out ESC-50 and FLEURS (43 languages) recordings, both models answer 95% to 97% of questions correctly. How does d1.2 score on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index? The index combines 6 evaluations. AA-Paperclip carries 30% of the weight. EvalSafe-O*NET-AA, AA-Omniscience-Decision v1.1, HLE-MultiChoice v1.1 and AA-Symmetry v1.1 carry 15% each. When2Call carries 10%. Its Decision Score penalizes confident wrong answers. On the AA chart shared by Liquid AI, d1.2-ultra scores 75. Drex Max v1.1, SubQ Snap 1.2 and GLiDE v1.2 follow at 73. d1.2 scores 69. That is 2 points below the deprecated d1-ultra at 71. Liquid AI argues no model scores higher than d1.2 for less money. How well calibrated are the probabilities? A calibrated model that says 80% is right about 80% of the time, so teams can route low-confidence cases to humans. articles.title: SKT, AI 기지국으로 일반 차량 무인 이송…2027년 KG모빌리티 공장 적용 추진
articles.content:
SK텔레콤(SKT)이 인공지능(AI) 기반 무선접속망(AI-RAN)을 활용해 자율주행 기능이 없는 일반 차량을 무인으로 이송하는 기술을 개발했다. 차량 자체가 아닌 통신 기지국에서 주변 환경을 인식하고 주행을 제어하는 방식으로, 2027년 실제 자동차 생산공장 물류 현장에 적용할 계획이다.

SKT는 과학기술정보통신부가 주최한 ‘제27회 전파방송 기술대상’에서 ‘AI-RAN 기반 완성차 무인 자율 이송 기술(AVM, Autonomous Vehicle Marshalling)’로 장관상을 수상했다고 18일 밝혔다. 이로써 2022년부터 5년 연속 장관상을 받았으며, 해당 기술은 지난달 ‘네트워크 엑스 어워드(Network X Awards)’에 이어 두 번째 수상 성과를 거뒀다.

이번 기술의 핵심은 AI-RAN 기지국이 차량의 주행 판단과 제어를 담당한다는 점이다. 현장에 설치된 라이다(LiDAR) 센서가 수집한 3차원 공간 데이터를 기지국으로 전송하면, AI가 디지털 트윈을 생성해 주변 상황을 분석하고 최적의 이동 경로를 계산한다. 이후 5G 단독모드(SA) 통신을 통해 차량에 조향·가속·감속·변속 명령을 전달한다.

SK텔레콤은 에치에프알(HFR), 서울로보틱스(Seoul Robotics)와 공동 실증을 진행해 센서 데이터 수집부터 AI 판단, 차량 제어까지 필요한 시간 안에 처리할 수 있음을 확인했다. 이를 통해 별도의 자율주행 기능이 없는 일반 차량도 외부 네트워크 기반으로 무인 이송할 수 있는 가능성을 검증했다.

현재는 정부의 ‘하이퍼 AI 네트워크 기반조성’ 실증사업과 연계해 판교 피지컬 AI 리빙랩에서 기술을 고도화하고 있다. 2027년에는 에릭슨(Ericsson)의 5G 기술을 적용한 AI-RAN 선도망을 KG모빌리티 평택공장에 구축해 실제 완성차 물류 환경에서 성능을 검증할 예정이다.

SK텔레콤은 오는 12월 9일부터 11일까지 인천 송도에서 열리는 ‘6G 비전 페스트 2026’에서 해당 기술을 공개할 계획이다.

류탁기 SK텔레콤 네트워크기술담당은 “AI-RAN 기반 무인 자율 이송 기술을 하이퍼 AI 과제를 통해 고도화해 실제 산업 현장에서 피지컬 AI 실행 인프라로서의 가능성을 증명해 나가겠다”고 말했다.
articles.summary: SK텔레콤이 차량 자체가 아닌 AI-RAN 기지국에서 환경 인식과 주행 제어를 수행하는 완성차 무인 이송 기술을 개발했다. 라이다의 3차원 데이터를 기반으로 디지털 트윈과 이동 경로를 생성하고, 5G 단독모드 통신으로 차량에 조향·가속·감속·변속 명령을 전달한다. HFR·서울로보틱스와의 실증에서 센서 수집부터 차량 제어까지 필요한 시간 안에 처리할 수 있음을 확인했다고 밝혔다. 2027년 KG모빌리티 평택공장에 선도망을 구축해 실제 물류 환경에서 검증할 계획으로, 현재 성과는 상용 운영 완료가 아니라 외부 네트워크 기반 무인 이송의 가능성 검증이다.

articles.title: NVIDIA Open-Sources NVKE and NVKR for Managed Kubernetes on GPU Infrastructure
articles.content: NVIDIA has released 2 open-source projects for running managed Kubernetes on GPU infrastructure: NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE) and NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes (NVKR). Both were recently announced as components of the NVIDIA DSX AI Factory Platform. NVKE is the control plane for a managed Kubernetes service. NVKR builds the OS images, container images and packages those clusters depend on. Both ship under Apache 2.0 and are in public preview. TL;DR Size / footprint: 3 CPU servers for the management cluster, 3 CPU servers per workload control plane, plus a pool of GPU worker nodes. A local evaluation needs 6 CPUs, 12 GiB RAM, 100 GiB disk and no GPU. Runs on: your own NVIDIA GPU bare-metal servers, provisioned through NVIDIA Infra Controller (NICo). Node images build for amd64 and arm64. Performance: no throughput or provisioning-time benchmarks are published. Quality signal is certification, not speed. Best: Certified Kubernetes AI Platform and Certified Kubernetes Installer, conformance tested on Kubernetes 1.36. Worst: after install, the NVKE API serves plain HTTP on port 30080 with authentication off, and there is no management-plane upgrade or backup procedure. Bottom line: best thing: open, attested, upstream Kubernetes for GPU clouds. Worst thing: preview-grade security and lifecycle gaps; not for production yet. What is NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE)? NVKE is open-source software that an AI factory installs to run a managed Kubernetes service on its own NVIDIA GPU infrastructure. The repo calls it ‘a self-hosting factory for Kubernetes clusters,’ not a distribution. It exposes a REST API and controllers on a management cluster. Customers get standard clusters and use kubectl. The operator manages them through the NVKE API or the nvkectl CLI. NVKE uses upstream Kubernetes, kubeadm and Cluster API. It is written in Go and has no runtime dependency on NVKR. What does NVIDIA Kubernetes Recipes (NVKR) do? NVKR is a build system with declarative Definitions. It produces executables, container images, Helm charts and node images for amd64 and arm64. ‘Recipes’ define validated combinations of software versions and GPU generations. Hosted workflows attach signatures, SBOMs and provenance to digest-pinned OCI references. NVKR can also build artifacts for other Kubernetes management systems. How does the NVKE architecture work? The NVIDIA technical blog walkthrough describes 5 stages: Bootstrap: nvkectl bootstrap site starts a temporary single-node kind cluster on a bootstrap host. Management cluster: NVKE requests 3 servers from NICo, which boots them from the node image. The temporary cluster is then deleted. Machine provisioning: NICo handles bare-metal lifecycle. CAPNICo, a Cluster API provider, connects NICo to NVKE. Release sets: operators publish a machine image, a cluster release and a node pool release. Customers pick a release by name. Workload clusters: each customer cluster has its own control plane, etcd and node pools. NVKE installs OVN-Kubernetes and NodeLocal DNSCache. A node must present an attested SPIFFE identity before it gets join credentials. The README says SPIRE uses TPM for this. Per-cluster etcd encryption is available. An OpenTelemetry-based Helm chart exports logs, metrics and traces over OTLP. Inside workload clusters, 3 companion projects plug in: AI Cluster Runtime (AICR) for the GPU runtime, NodeWright for node packages and NVSentinel for break-fix automation. && How does NVKE compare with Gardener and Kamaji? NVKE + NVKR (NVIDIA)Gardener (SAP)Kamaji (Clastix)What it isManaged Kubernetes management plane plus artifact builderKubernetes clusters as a serviceHosted control plane managerControl plane modelDedicated per cluster: own control plane, etcd, node poolsRuns as pods in seed clustersRuns as pods; shared Datastore possibleTarget infrastructureNVIDIA GPU bare metal via NICoAWS, Azure, GCP, OpenStack, Alicloud (conformance table); extensibleWorks alongside Cluster API providersLicenseApache 2.0Apache 2.0Apache 2.0ConformanceCertified Kubernetes AI Platform and Installer; tested on 1.36Certified up to v1.35Described as CNCF-compliantNode identitySPIFFE/SPIRE attestation with TPMNot disclosedNot disclosedSigned build pipelineYes (NVKR: signatures, SBOMs, provenance)Not disclosedNot disclosedMaturityPublic preview, not for productionSelf-described production-readyNot disclosed Who is adopting NVKE and NVKR? NVIDIA Cloud Partners Firmus and SK Telecom are integrating both projects into AI factories. Mirantis, Rafay, Spectro Cloud, OpenNebula Systems and vCluster are adding components to managed Kubernetes offerings. Netris is enabling NVKE for its network automation. How do you try NVKE? A local quickstart runs on 1 Linux host or VM, amd64 or arm64. It needs at least 6 CPUs, 12 GiB free memory, 100 GiB free disk, Docker and virtual TPM support. No GPU or NVIDIA account is required. A real install needs a NICo deployment with enrolled capacity, a build host with KVM, an HTTP server and a registry. NVKR has no qualified Release yet. Key Takeaways NVKE manages clusters; NVKR builds and signs what they run. Both are Apache 2.0, in public preview, not for production. Conformance tested on Kubernetes 1.36, with TPM-attested node identity. Default API is HTTP on port 30080 with auth off. Local evaluation needs 6 CPUs, 12 GiB RAM and no GPU. articles.title: Sarvam Launches Sarvam Token Factory: Bringing India-Hosted Inference to 8 Open Models
articles.content: Sarvam has opened Sarvam Token Factory to everyone. Sarvam Token Factory is an inference platform from Sarvam that serves its own models and open-weight models from GPU clusters in India. Developers reach every model through one OpenAI-compatible API. For India-based teams, this means low-latency tokens without sending traffic to overseas clouds. You can check the deployment options and specs here through our GPULeaderboard.com chrome extension. TL;DR Size: 8 models listed at launch, including Sarvam 105B (105B total, 9B active, 128K context), GLM 5.3, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, Kimi K3.1 Pro and Gemma 4 31B. Runs on: NVIDIA B200 clusters in India. Sarvam 105B now fits on 1 B200 per replica. On-premise deployment is offered to enterprises. Performance: Fastest first token from Mumbai on most tested cases, per Sarvam’s own measurements. Best: Kimi K3.1 Pro at 6,177 tokens/s per GPU vs 3,213 for InferenceX, at 70 tokens/s per user (1.9x). What is Sarvam Token Factory? It is a managed inference stack, not a single model. Sarvam first previewed it as Sarvam Inference at its Epoch event. The launch post lists 8 models: Sarvam 105B, GLM 5.3, GLM 5.3 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Kimi K3, Kimi K3.1 Pro and Gemma 4 31B. The docs split them into 2 groups. Pay-as-you-go models run on shared endpoints. DeepSeek V4 Pro, Kimi K3.1 Pro, Qwen 3.8 27B, Clef and EmbeddingGemma 2 need Provisioned Throughput, enabled per organisation. How does it work? The stack has 3 layers around a shared cache: Control plane: a cache-aware router, admission control and a planner. Inference engine: separate GPU pools for prefill and decode. Cache: GPU memory plus a shared G3 store built on Mooncake. It builds on vLLM, SGLang, Dynamo, Mooncake, NIXL, DeepEP, DeepGEMM and FlashInfer. An orchestrator agent proposes experiments, and an engineer approves each deployment. Caching drives most of the gains. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash serves 450B+ tokens per day, with 95.7% of prompt tokens served from cache. On GLM 5.3, the planner cut prefill GPU-hours from 32.3 to 17.1 under the same replayed load. For Sarvam 105B, MXFP8 weights plus speculative decoding raised output throughput about 2.2x. That cut each replica from 2 B200s to 1. Sarvam says none of these changes reduced accuracy. How fast is it? Benchmarks All numbers below come from Sarvam’s launch post. They are self-reported. Sarvam 105B: 0.2 s first token and 330 tokens/s for a single user. Gemma 4 31B (10K prompt, Mumbai): 0.40 s first token and 308 tokens/s, vs 2.00 s and 193 tokens/s at the only other provider. Kimi K3.1 Pro (16 B200s): 6,177 vs 3,213 tokens/s per GPU against InferenceX at 70 tokens/s per user. Heavy agent load (72 sessions): median first token 0.8 s vs 11.6 s for InferenceX. GLM 5.3 Flash (64 sessions): p99 first token 3.2 s vs 14.1 s for stock vLLM and Dynamo. The results are not a clean sweep. On DeepSeek V4.1 Flash with a 10K prompt, Together posts 0.71 s first token vs Sarvam’s 0.90 s. Together also streams faster, at 278 tokens/s vs 130 on Sarvam Standard. articles.summary: Sarvam이 인도 내 NVIDIA B200 클러스터에서 자사 모델과 공개 가중치 모델을 제공하는 Token Factory를 전면 공개했다. 출시 목록에는 8개 모델이 포함되며, 개발자는 OpenAI 호환 API로 접근하고 기업은 온프레미스 배포도 선택할 수 있다. 프리필과 디코드 GPU 풀을 분리하고 공유 캐시와 캐시 인식 라우팅을 결합한 구조로, 회사 측은 특정 Kimi 모델 조건에서 비교 대상 대비 약 1.9배의 GPU당 처리량을 제시했다. 인도 내 데이터 처리와 지연 시간 최적화를 겨냥한 서비스이며, 성능 수치는 공급사 측정이고 일부 모델에는 별도 처리량 예약이 필요하다.

articles.title: 컨테이너처럼 쓰고, VM처럼 격리하기 3편 - Fabric Manager 파티션과 DRA를 이용한 GPU 할당
articles.content: 2편에서는 GPU를 vfio-pci에 바인딩해 VM에 연결하는 구조와 GPU 8장 VM의 부팅·메모리 구성을 살펴봤습니다. 이번 3편에서는 그 VM에 연결할 GPU를 어떻게 고르는지 다룹니다. 이 연재는 다음과 같이 구성됩니다. 1편: 컨테이너와 VM의 차이, Kata Containers의 Pod 실행 구조 2편: GPU 패스스루 계층과 GPU 8장 VM의 부팅·메모리 구성 3편: Fabric Manager 파티션과 DRA를 이용한 GPU 할당 4편: IB 네트워크와 로컬 NVMe, vCPU 배치, 베어메탈 대비 성능 GPU 8장이 장착된 서버에서 사용자에게 GPU 2장을 제공할 때 아무 2장이나 고를 수는 없습니다. GPU 간 고속 통신에 쓰는 NVLink가 하드웨어에서 허용한 조합끼리만 연결되기 때문입니다. 이 연결 규칙을 Kubernetes의 GPU 할당에 반영하려고 장치 플러그인(device plugin)으로 여러 방법을 시도해 봤지만 원하는 조합을 보장하지 못했고, 결국 DRA(동적 리소스 할당)로 바꿔 자체 드라이버를 만들었습니다. 이번 편에서는 이 과정에 이어 사용자가 GPU를 요청하는 방법과 할당된 GPU를 VM에 연결하는 과정, 할당 결과를 다룹니다. 아무 GPU나 묶을 수 없는 이유 사용자가 GPU 2장을 요청하면 8장 가운데 어떤 2장을 제공해야 할까요? NVLink로 묶을 수 있는 GPU 조합이 어떻게 정해지는지 살펴보겠습니다. GPU 간 통신과 NVLink 모델이 GPU 한 장의 메모리에 들어가지 않거나 학습을 빠르게 하려면 작업을 여러 GPU에 나눠야 합니다. 작업을 나눠 맡은 GPU들은 학습 스텝마다 계산 결과를 주고받는데, 대표적인 연산은 각 GPU의 그레이디언트(gradient)를 모두 더해 나누어 갖는 NCCL(NVIDIA Collective Communications Library)의 all_reduce입니다. 이 통신이 느리면 학습도 느려집니다. PCIe만으로는 GPU 8장이 동시에 데이터를 주고받기에 대역폭이 부족하므로 GPU 전용 연결인 NVLink를 씁니다. 네이버 클라우드에서 구성한 B200 서버에서는 보드의 NVSwitch 칩이 GPU 8장을 NVLink로 연결합니다. Fabric Manager가 정하는 파티션 NVSwitch가 어떤 GPU끼리 연결할지는 호스트에서 실행되는 NVIDIA Fabric Manager가 정합니다. VM 환경에서는 NVSwitch를 호스트에 남겨 두는 Shared NVSwitch 모드로 Fabric Manager를 실행합니다. Fabric Manager는 NVLink로 함께 묶을 수 있는 GPU 조합을 미리 정해 두는데 이 조합을 fabric partition(이하 '파티션')이라고 합니다. 디스크를 나누는 파티션이나 GPU 한 장을 여러 개로 나누는 MIG(Multi-Instance GPU)와 달리 여러 GPU를 하나로 묶는 단위입니다. VM에 GPU 2장을 연결할 때는 그 2장으로 이루어진 파티션을 활성화합니다. 그러면 두 GPU 사이에만 NVLink 경로가 구성되고 다른 VM의 GPU와는 연결되지 않습니다. 같은 GPU를 포함한 두 파티션은 동시에 활성화할 수 없습니다. B200 서버 한 대에서 Fabric Manager가 보고한 파티션은 GPU 8장짜리 1개, 4장짜리 2개, 2장짜리 4개, 1장짜리 8개였습니다. 이름 크기 포함하는 물리 GPU id1-8gpu 8 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8 id2-4gpu-1234 4 1 2 3 4 id3-4gpu-5678 4 5 6 7 8 id4-2gpu-12 2 1 2 id5-2gpu-34 2 3 4 id6-2gpu-56 2 5 6 id7-2gpu-78 2 7 8 id8-1gpu-1 ~ id15-1gpu-8 1 GPU 하나씩 8개 여기서 GPU 번호는 Fabric Manager의 물리 GPU 번호를 뜻하며 PCI 주소 순서와 일치하지 않습니다. 파티션 목록도 서버마다 Fabric Manager가 보고하는 값이기 때문에 위 표를 다른 보드에 그대로 적용할 수는 없습니다. GPU를 VM에 나누어 주려면 요청한 수량에 맞으면서 이미 사용 중인 GPU가 없는 파티션을 골라야 합니다. 예를 들어 GPU 1·2는 2장짜리 파티션 하나를 이루므로 한 VM에 함께 연결할 수 있지만, GPU 2·3은 서로 다른 2장짜리 파티션에 걸쳐 있어 2장짜리 VM 하나에 함께 연결할 수 없습니다. 장치 플러그인으로 파티션을 고르려던 시도 그런데 Kubernetes는 이 파티션 규칙을 모릅니다. Kubernetes에서 GPU Pod를 만들 때는 보통 컨테이너의 resources에 GPU 개수를 적습니다. resources: limits: nvidia.com/gpu: 1 장치 플러그인 방식에서 스케줄러는 노드의 남은 GPU 개수만 보고 Pod를 배치합니다. 어느 GPU를 연결할지는 Pod가 배치된 노드의 kubelet과 플러그인이 정하므로 Pod를 만든 사람이나 스케줄러는 GPU 선택에 관여할 수 없습니다. GPU를 한 장씩 쓰는 워크로드라면 개수만 요청해도 충분합니다. 하지만 저희는 한 VM에 연결할 GPU를 같은 파티션에서 골라야 했으므로 GPU를 고르는 과정에 개입할 방법이 필요했습니다. NVIDIA의 샌드박스 장치 플러그인은 패스스루용 GPU를 nvidia.com/pgpu라는 이름으로 Kubernetes에 알립니다. 처음에는 이 플러그인을 바탕으로 파티션 제약을 반영할 방법을 찾았습니다. 기본 플러그인, Pod 어노테이션, 플러그인 포크를 차례로 시도했지만 세 방법 모두 파티션 단위 할당을 보장하지 못했습니다. 방법 결과 기본 장치 플러그인으로 nvidia.com/pgpu: 4 요청 파티션을 고려하지 않고 배정한 4장이 활성화된 파티션과 맞지 않아 CUDA 초기화 실패(cudaErrorSystemNotReady, 802) Pod 어노테이션으로 CDI(Container Device Interface) 디바이스를 직접 지정 kubelet이 어노테이션을 컨테이너 요청에 반영하지 않아 지정한 GPU가 VM에 연결되지 않음 플러그인을 포크해 GetPreferredAllocation()으로 파티션에 맞는 조합을 추천 플러그인이 추천을 내지 못하면 kubelet은 경고 없이 기본 배정으로 전환. Pod가 삭제되어 GPU가 반납되어도 플러그인에 알리는 API가 없음 장치 플러그인 API로는 GPU를 개수가 아닌 파티션 단위로 고르고 해제할 방법이 없었습니다. Kubernetes 커뮤니티도 장치 플러그인 API를 확장하기보다 새 API인 DRA를 개발하는 방향을 택했으므로 저희도 GPU 할당을 DRA로 바꾸기로 했습니다. 이때 같은 GPU가 두 경로로 등록되지 않도록 nvidia.com/pgpu를 알리던 샌드박스 장치 플러그인은 클러스터에서 제거했습니다. PVC처럼 디바이스를 요청하는 DRA DRA는 디바이스를 요청하고 준비하는 과정을 PV(PersistentVolume)·PVC(PersistentVolumeClaim)와 비슷한 구조로 다루는 API입니다. 노드는 보유한 디바이스의 이름과 속성을 함께 알리고 Pod는 개수 대신 'GPU 2장으로 이루어진 파티션 하나'처럼 필요한 디바이스의 조건을 요청합니다. 스토리지 API와 비교하면 다음과 같습니다. 스토리지 DRA 의미 StorageClass DeviceClass 어떤 종류의 디바이스인지, 어느 드라이버가 관리하는지 PersistentVolumeClaim ResourceClaim 워크로드가 요청한 자원과 실제로 배정된 자원 PV 목록 ResourceSlice 드라이버가 이 노드에서 보유한 디바이스 목록과 속성·용량 CSI(Container Storage Interface)의 마운트 NodePrepareResources 선택된 디바이스를 그 노드에서 실제로 쓸 수 있게 준비 디바이스 하나가 Pod에 할당되기까지 드라이버, 사용자, 스케줄러, kubelet이 차례로 관여합니다. 장치 플러그인과의 가장 큰 차이는 디바이스를 고르는 주체입니다. 장치 플러그인에서는 노드의 kubelet이 고르지만 DRA에서는 클러스터의 스케줄러가 고릅니다. 앞에서 장치 플러그인으로 막혔던 항목을 DRA와 나란히 놓으면 다음과 같습니다. 항목 장치 플러그인 DRA 노드가 알리는 것 개수 디바이스 이름과 속성 목록 요청에 적는 것 nvidia.com/gpu: 1 CEL 조건식과 개수 고르는 주체 노드의 kubelet 스케줄러 상호 배제 표현 불가 SharedCounters 디바이스 간 관계 표현 불가 constraints로 표현 해제 API 없음 NodeUnprepareResources ResourceClaim(이하 '클레임')의 조건은 CEL(Common Expression Language)로 device.attributes['...'].size == 8처럼 디바이스 속성을 비교해 적습니다. 여러 디바이스가 같은 속성 값을 갖도록 묶을 때는 constraints의 matchAttribute를 씁니다. 자체 DRA 드라이버를 만든 이유 API를 정했으니 디바이스를 발행하고 준비할 드라이버가 필요했습니다. 공개된 DRA 드라이버부터 검토했지만, 저희는 호스트 GPU를 항상 vfio-pci에 바인딩해 두기 때문에 그대로 쓸 수 없었습니다. 드라이버 맞지 않은 이유 kubernetes-sigs/dra-driver-nvidia-gpu VFIO(Virtual Function I/O)와 Fabric Manager를 지원하지만 GPU를 호스트 NVIDIA 드라이버의 NVML(NVIDIA Management Library)로 찾으므로 호스트에 GPU 드라이버가 없는 환경에서는 쓸 수 없음 kubernetes-sigs/dranet NIC를 Pod의 네트워크 네임스페이스로 옮기는 방식. vfio-pci에 바인딩된 NIC는 할당 대상에서 제외 두 드라이버를 각각 포크해 함께 쓰는 방법도 있었지만 같은 PCIe 스위치의 GPU와 NIC(network interface card)를 묶어 할당하는 기능은 여전히 따로 구현해야 했습니다. 그래서 GPU와 NIC를 한 드라이버에서 관리하는 자체 DRA 드라이버를 만들었습니다. 자체 드라이버는 노드마다 하나씩 실행되는 kubelet 플러그인입니다. 파티션뿐 아니라 GPU와 같은 PCIe 스위치에 연결된 IB(InfiniBand) NIC도 디바이스로 발행합니다. NIC 디바이스는 4편에서 다루고, 이번 편에서는 파티션을 중심으로 설명합니다. 겹치는 파티션의 동시 할당 막기 드라이버는 Fabric Manager가 보고한 파티션 15개를 DRA 디바이스 15개로 그대로 발행했습니다. 이 글에서는 파티션 하나를 나타내는 이 DRA 디바이스를 '파티션 디바이스'라고 부릅니다. 디바이스 이름에는 앞의 파티션 표처럼 파티션 번호와 GPU 구성을 넣었고, CEL 조건에 쓸 수 있도록 size(GPU 수)와 fmPartitionId(Fabric Manager의 파티션 번호)를 속성으로 붙였습니다. 남은 문제는 같은 GPU를 포함한 파티션 디바이스가 동시에 할당되지 않게 하는 것이었습니다. 여기에는 DRA의 SharedCounters를 사용했습니다. 물리 GPU마다 용량 1인 카운터를 발행하고 각 파티션 디바이스가 자신에게 포함된 GPU의 카운터를 1씩 소비하도록 선언했습니다. 스케줄러는 디바이스를 고를 때 카운터의 남은 용량을 계산합니다. 두 파티션 디바이스가 같은 GPU의 카운터를 요구하면 용량을 초과하므로 동시에 할당할 수 없습니다. 예를 들어 B200 서버에서 id2-4gpu-1234를 할당하면 GPU 14의 카운터가 모두 소진됩니다. 그러면 GPU 14 중 하나라도 포함한 id1-8gpu, id4-2gpu-12, id5-2gpu-34와 GPU 1~4의 1장짜리 파티션 디바이스는 배정 대상에서 빠집니다. 겹치는 GPU가 없는 id3-4gpu-5678은 같은 노드에서 함께 쓸 수 있습니다. 상호 배제는 스케줄러의 카운터 계산으로 보장하므로 드라이버가 겹치지 않는 조합을 고를 필요는 없습니다. 드라이버는 NodePrepareResources에서 이미 준비된 클레임과 겹치지 않는지 한 번 더 확인할 뿐입니다. 이 카운터를 쓰려면 Kubernetes의 DRAPartitionableDevices 기능 게이트를 활성화해야 합니다. 파티션 준비, 해제, 상태 복구 디바이스가 선택되면 kubelet은 NodePrepareResources를 호출합니다. 드라이버는 Fabric Manager의 현재 상태를 확인해 비활성 파티션을 활성화하고 물리 GPU 번호를 PCI 주소로 변환해 VFIO 장치 파일을 찾습니다. 이어 클레임마다 CDI 스펙 파일을 하나씩 작성합니다. 2편에서 본 파일이 이때 만들어집니다. 사용이 끝나 kubelet이 NodeUnprepareResources를 호출하면 CDI 스펙을 삭제하고 Fabric Manager에서 파티션을 비활성화합니다. 파티션 목록은 서버마다 다르므로 드라이버에 하드코딩하지 않고 각 노드의 Fabric Manager에서 가져옵니다. Fabric Manager에 연결할 수 없거나 목록이 비어 있으면 파티션 디바이스를 발행하지 않고, 그동안 GPU를 요청한 Pod는 Pending 상태로 기다립니다. 오래된 목록으로 발행하면 활성화할 수 없는 파티션의 디바이스를 스케줄러가 고르고 Pod를 해당 노드에 배치해, 그 노드에서 클레임 준비가 실패할 수 있기 때문입니다. 발행 후에도 60초마다 IB NIC 탐색과 파티션 조회를 반복해 바뀐 목록을 드라이버 재시작 없이 반영합니다. 드라이버를 재시작해도 실행 중인 게스트의 파티션은 유지되어야 합니다. 그래서 드라이버는 시작할 때 자기 노드의 클레임을 읽고, 클레임이 있는데 비활성인 파티션을 다시 활성화합니다. 반대로 클레임이 없는 활성 파티션은 다른 주체가 활성화했을 수도 있으므로 경고만 기록하고 비활성화하지 않습니다. Fabric Manager를 재시작하면 실행 중이던 CUDA 작업이 종료되고 활성 파티션도 해제되므로 Fabric Manager는 실행 중인 게스트가 없을 때만 재시작해야 합니다. 사용자가 GPU를 요청하는 방법 사용자가 파티션 규칙이나 CEL까지 알아야 한다면 GPU를 쓰기 어렵습니다. 그래서 클러스터 관리자가 사용자 네임스페이스에 ResourceClaimTemplate으로 GPU 조건을 정의해 두고, 사용자는 템플릿 이름만 참조하게 했습니다. 아래 템플릿은 size가 8인 파티션 디바이스 1개를 요청합니다. 파티션 디바이스만 고르는 조건은 DeviceClass에 들어 있습니다. apiVersion: resource.k8s.io/v1 kind: ResourceClaimTemplate metadata: name: example-8gpu spec: spec: devices: requests: - name: gpu exactly: deviceClassName: kata-gpu.nks.ncloud.com count: 1 selectors: - cel: expression: "device.attributes['kata-gpu.nks.ncloud.com'].size == 8" 사용자는 Pod 스펙의 resourceClaims에 템플릿 이름을 적고 컨테이너의 claims에서 참조하면 됩니다. Pod를 생성하면 Kubernetes가 템플릿으로 클레임을 하나 만들고 Pod를 삭제할 때 함께 지우므로 사용자가 클레임을 따로 생성하거나 삭제할 필요는 없습니다. spec: resourceClaims: - name: gpu resourceClaimTemplateName: example-8gpu containers: - name: app resources: claims: - name: gpu 이렇게 요청한 GPU 하나는 DRA, containerd, QEMU 계층마다 다른 이름으로 표시됩니다. 할당된 GPU를 VM에 연결하는 kata shim 스케줄러가 고른 GPU는 어떻게 VM 안으로 들어갈까요? GPU는 VM이 부팅할 때 콜드 플러그로 연결해야 하는데, 업스트림 Kata Containers(이하 'kata')에는 DRA로 할당한 하드웨어를 콜드 플러그하는 경로가 없었습니다. kata shim은 샌드박스를 만들면서 kubelet의 PodResources API로 Pod에 할당된 디바이스를 조회합니다. 그런데 업스트림 shim은 응답에서 장치 플러그인이 할당한 디바이스만 읽고 DRA가 할당한 디바이스(DynamicResources)는 읽지 않아서 VM이 GPU 없이 부팅되었습니다. containerd가 CDI로 OCI(Open Container Initiative) 스펙에 VFIO 장치 정보를 넣어 주기는 하지만 이 정보는 샌드박스 부팅 후 컨테이너를 만들 때 도착하므로 콜드 플러그에는 너무 늦습니다. 내부 수정본에서는 kata shim이 PodResources API의 DRA 디바이스 목록을 클레임 단위로 읽어 GPU와 NIC를 정해진 순서대로 루트 포트에 연결합니다. 4편에서 다룰 NCCL 토폴로지 파일을 만들 때 이 순서를 기준으로 게스트의 PCI 주소를 미리 계산하기 때문입니다. 이 수정은 업스트림에 PR #13323(Go 런타임)과 PR #13420(runtime-rs)으로 제안했습니다. 서버 한 대를 VM 4개로 나누어 실행 파티션 할당과 VM 연결을 갖춘 뒤 B200 서버 한 대에서 GPU 1장, 1장, 2장, 4장을 각각 연결한 VM 4개를 동시에 실행했습니다. 이 상태에서 GPU 2장·4장 VM의 NCCL all_reduce 버스 대역폭(NCCL이 계산하는 busbw)을 측정했습니다. 비교를 위해 GPU 8장 VM 하나만 실행한 경우도 측정했고, 메시지 크기는 모두 8GiB입니다. 베어메탈 값은 같은 노드를 일반 컨테이너 환경으로 바꿔 같은 GPU 조합으로 측정했습니다. 조건 kata 게스트 버스 대역폭 베어메탈 컨테이너 버스 대역폭 2장, 1+1+2+4 동시 실행 중 623.5GB/s 629.7GB/s 4장, 1+1+2+4 동시 실행 중 680.7GB/s 683.3GB/s 8장 단독 835.9GB/s 839.7GB/s 세 경우 모두 kata 게스트의 버스 대역폭은 베어메탈과의 차이가 1% 이내였습니다. 할당 결과를 확인하는 방법 할당이 의도대로 되었는지는 ResourceSlice와 ResourceClaim, 그리고 게스트 안의 NCCL 테스트로 확인할 수 있습니다. 먼저 B200 서버 한 대의 ResourceSlice를 조회하면 Fabric Manager가 보고한 파티션 15개에 대응하는 파티션 디바이스가 그대로 나옵니다. $ kubectl get resourceslices --field-selector spec.nodeName=<node> \ -o jsonpath='{range .items[*].spec.devices[*]}{.name}{"\n"}{end}' | grep gpu | grep -v rails id1-8gpu id2-4gpu-1234 id3-4gpu-5678 id4-2gpu-12 id5-2gpu-34 id6-2gpu-56 id7-2gpu-78 id8-1gpu-1 id9-1gpu-2 id10-1gpu-3 id11-1gpu-4 id12-1gpu-5 id13-1gpu-6 id14-1gpu-7 id15-1gpu-8 Pod에 배정된 디바이스는 ResourceClaim의 status에 기록됩니다. 아래는 파티션 디바이스만 요청한 클레임의 출력입니다. $ kubectl get resourceclaims -A \ -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\t"}{.status.allocation.devices.results[*].device}{"\n"}{end}' <claim 이름> id4-2gpu-12 게스트 안에서는 nccl-tests의 all_reduce_perf로 NVLink 통신을 확인합니다. 아래는 B200 GPU 8장 VM에서 실행한 출력입니다. $ all_reduce_perf -b 512M -e 8G -f 2 -g 8 -n 20 # nccl-tests version 2.19.7 nccl-headers=22501 nccl-library=22501 ... 536870912 134217728 float sum -1 1321.87 406.15 710.75 0 1316.15 407.91 713.84 0 1073741824 268435456 float sum -1 2550.64 420.97 736.7
articles.summary: 네이버 클라우드가 B200 서버의 NVLink 연결 제약을 Kubernetes GPU 할당에 반영하기 위해 자체 DRA 드라이버를 구현한 사례를 공개했다. 기존 장치 플러그인 방식으로는 원하는 GPU 조합을 보장하지 못해, Fabric Manager가 허용하는 GPU 묶음을 할당 단위로 사용했다. Shared NVSwitch 모드에서는 스위치를 호스트에 남기고 해당 묶음 내부에만 NVLink 경로를 구성해 VM별 GPU 연결을 분리한다. 여러 사용자가 GPU 서버를 공유할 때 고속 통신과 격리를 함께 설계하는 참고 사례이며, 허용되는 조합은 서버별 Fabric Manager 정보를 확인해야 한다.

articles.title: Minari: Infrastructure for Collaborative Reinforcement Learning Datasets
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.18644v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Offline reinforcement learning (RL) depends on shared datasets, but sharing them is still hard. Each benchmark ships its own format, documentation is thin, and most datasets cannot be regenerated once the environment code moves on. We introduce Minari, an open-source Python library for creating, sharing, and loading RL datasets. Its API follows Gymnasium, so recording a dataset means wrapping an environment and stepping through it as usual. From there, users can attach metadata, filter, combine, and shuffle datasets, and publish or download them with one command through the HuggingFace Hub. Every dataset stores the environment specification, seeds, applied wrappers, and pinned package requirements needed to rebuild the environment and regenerate the data. TorchRL, AgileRL, and d3rlpy already load Minari datasets natively, so switching datasets in those libraries takes one line of code. Minari also hosts 338 reproducible datasets (350K trajectories, 55M steps) covering robotic locomotion and manipulation, maze and grid navigation, language-conditioned instruction following, Atari, and web navigation, including a full regeneration of D4RL with public generation scripts. We report baseline scores for six offline RL algorithms on the regenerated D4RL and MuJoCo datasets.
articles.summary: Minari는 강화학습 데이터를 생성·공유·로드하는 오픈소스 Python 라이브러리로, Gymnasium 환경을 감싸 기존 실행 과정에서 데이터를 기록한다. 환경 명세, 시드, 래퍼, 고정된 패키지 요구사항을 함께 보관해 환경 코드가 바뀐 뒤에도 데이터를 재생성할 수 있도록 설계됐다. 연구진은 338개 재현 가능한 데이터셋에 35만 개 궤적과 5,500만 스텝을 제공하며, TorchRL·AgileRL·d3rlpy의 기본 연동도 소개했다. 오프라인 강화학습에서 제각각인 데이터 형식과 재현성 문제를 줄이는 실용적인 공통 인프라다.

articles.title: Instructor-designed AI improves learning in a randomized trial across 19 universities
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.19099v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Universities are alarmed by recent evidence that artificial intelligence (AI) can undermine learning, with students prescribed generic chatbots or centrally designed AI tools performing worse. In a pre-registered randomized controlled trial across 7,200 students at 19 universities over three semesters, we tested whether AI designed by frontline instructors can improve learning. We encouraged instructors to design AI solutions they believed would best help their students. Drawing on their unique knowledge of their classes and students, the instructors created a wide array of innovations. We show that these instructor-designed AI innovations improved student learning, measured by AI-proof assessments (proctored, in-person examinations). We found no change in student engagement, measured by course activity records, or satisfaction, measured by course evaluations. Our findings demonstrate that AI can improve student learning when its adoption is frontline-driven, with instructors empowered to design and refine AI solutions for their own classrooms.
articles.summary: 19개 대학의 학생 7,200명을 대상으로 세 학기 동안 진행한 사전 등록 무작위 대조시험에서, 담당 교수가 설계한 AI 활용 방식이 학습 성과를 개선한 것으로 보고됐다. 교수들이 수업과 학생의 특성에 맞춰 도구를 설계했으며, 성과는 감독이 있는 대면 시험으로 측정했다. 반면 수업 활동 기록으로 본 참여도와 강의 평가로 본 만족도에는 변화가 없었다. 일괄적인 챗봇 도입보다 현장 교육자가 활용 방식을 설계하는 접근의 가능성을 보여주지만, 제공된 초록에는 학습 개선의 구체적인 효과 크기가 없다.

articles.title: Video-as-Experience: Learning Computer Use via Audio-Visual Understanding
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.18747v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multimodal large language models (LLMs) have enabled capable computer-use agents that perceive graphical user interfaces, reason over instructions, and execute actions. However, existing approaches to learning from video demonstrations typically convert videos into screenshot-based action trajectories, rather than directly leveraging their rich audio-visual information. We introduce VEX (Video as EXperience), a framework that uses audio-visual understanding to unify learning from external demonstrations and reflecting on an agent's own behavior. Following a watch-act-rewatch paradigm, the agent extracts procedural guidance from tutorial videos containing visual demonstrations and spoken explanations, executes tasks, and verifies its progress by rewatching its execution as video. We instantiate VEX with video-SALMONN-VEX, a 9B-scale audio-visual computer-use agent built on the video-SALMONN 2 architecture with a Qwen3.5-9B backbone. We further introduce Action-Grounded Guide Optimization (AGGO), a reinforcement learning method that optimizes video-derived guidance for downstream action prediction, and augment AgentNet, OSWorld, and CUA-Gym with over 24K real-world tutorial videos. Experiments on OSWorld and a complementary subset of CUA-Gym demonstrate consistent improvements, with video-SALMONN-VEX achieving a 22% relative increase in task success over its Qwen3.5 backbone on OSWorld. Moreover, its generated guidance improves Gemini-3.5-flash by 10% relatively on OSWorld. These results highlight the potential of audio-visual understanding as a unified interface for procedural learning and self-verification in computer-use agents.
articles.summary: VEX는 튜토리얼의 화면과 음성 설명을 함께 이해하고, 작업 실행 후 자신의 수행 영상을 다시 확인하는 컴퓨터 사용 에이전트 프레임워크다. 연구진은 Qwen3.5-9B 기반 모델과 영상에서 추출한 절차 지침을 행동 예측에 맞춰 최적화하는 강화학습 기법 AGGO를 제안하고, 기존 환경에 2만4,000개 이상의 실제 튜토리얼 영상을 추가했다. OSWorld에서 기반 모델 대비 작업 성공률이 상대적으로 22% 상승했으며, 생성한 지침을 Gemini-3.5-flash에 적용했을 때도 상대적으로 10% 개선됐다고 보고했다. 영상을 단순 스크린샷 행동열로 변환하는 대신 시청각 정보를 학습과 자기 검증에 직접 활용한다는 점이 의미 있다.

articles.title: Agents Cannot Hand Over What They Have Not Yet Understood
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.18642v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agents that work beyond a single context window, or in teams, hand their work to a successor as a short written summary. Evaluation has focused on whether an agent can solve a task, and relatively little is known about how much of what an agent has learned survives being written down. We study this in 56 interactive worlds with hidden rules, where an agent that is told nothing fails and an agent given a 300-character statement of the rules succeeds. We compare one agent that plays eight lives and keeps its whole history with a chain of eight agents that each play one life and inherit a 300-character note. All six models we test learn less in the chain: after eight generations it stands where the single agent stood after about four lives. Controlled variants of the chain decompose this handoff loss into three components: none from changing the agent, a smaller loss from compressing to 300 characters, and a larger loss from compressing repeatedly. When each note is written from the full record of earlier lives instead of from the previous note, the same 300 characters recover 70% to 82% of the loss. The loss is robust across model sizes and is not alleviated by instructing the writer to record evidence, to revise the inherited note, or to keep a structured ledger. In simpler terms, an agent cannot hand over what it has not yet understood: a note holds what its writer has worked out, and a rule that takes several lives to see is lost with the lives that were not passed on.
articles.summary: 숨겨진 규칙을 학습하는 56개 상호작용 환경에서, 에이전트가 짧은 인수인계 메모를 반복 전달하면 전체 기록을 유지하는 단일 에이전트보다 학습이 크게 저하되는 현상이 보고됐다. 시험한 6개 모델 모두에서 8세대의 에이전트 연쇄가 학습한 수준은 단일 에이전트가 약 4회 경험한 수준에 머물렀다. 손실의 주원인은 에이전트 교체 자체보다 반복 압축이었으며, 이전 메모 대신 전체 과거 기록에서 같은 300자 메모를 작성하면 손실의 70~82%를 회복했다. 장기 에이전트 시스템에서는 요약 형식 개선만이 아니라 원본 경험 기록을 보존하고 다시 참조하는 구조가 중요함을 시사한다.

articles.title: RSIMed: Scaling Medical Foundation Models beyond Limited Clinical Data via Retrieval-Grounded Self-Evolution
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.18646v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Rare diseases are hard to diagnose, and the labeled clinical records needed to train models for them are few, private, and slow to extend, since a specialist must read every case. A model that writes its own training tasks could learn beyond these records, but no program can check a model-written diagnosis, and a wrong answer key corrupts training. To tackle this dilemma between data scarcity and difficulty of data annotations, we introduce RSIMed, Recursive Self-Improvement in Medicine, one of the first self-evolving pipelines in which a task proposer co-evolves in context with a diagnostic solver on real clinical records. Seeded by training admissions, a frozen copy of the solver writes each clinical question from retrieved medical evidence, so its answer rests on a source, and steers topics and difficulty toward what the solver still gets wrong. On rare-disease diagnosis from MIMIC-IV admissions, the accuracy of RSIMed-27B grows linearly with training compute, while a static pool of generated tasks collapses. Without any external model, RSIMed-27B and RSIMed-9B reach 0.516 and 0.488 diagnostic accuracy, above every off-the-shelf GPT-5.6 setting, whose best reaches 0.399 at 38 times the inference cost of RSIMed-27B. Tasks written by four external teachers, including GPT-5.5, train a less accurate diagnostician than the solver's own. Trained only on diagnosis, RSIMed-RL-27B also improves on the physician-written tasks of HealthBench Professional, from 0.291 to 0.303 in adjusted score.
articles.summary: RSIMed는 검색한 의학 근거를 바탕으로 임상 질문을 만들고, 진단 모델이 어려워하는 주제와 난도에 맞춰 학습 과제를 갱신하는 자기 개선 파이프라인이다. 연구진은 MIMIC-IV 입원 기록 기반 희귀질환 진단에서 27B·9B 모델의 정확도가 각각 0.516과 0.488로, 비교한 GPT-5.6 설정의 최고치 0.399를 넘었다고 보고했다. 고정된 합성 과제 집합과 달리 학습 연산량 증가에 따라 성능이 향상됐으며, 진단 학습만으로 별도의 HealthBench Professional 점수도 소폭 개선됐다. 임상 데이터 부족을 완화할 가능성을 보여주지만, 특정 데이터셋에서의 결과를 실제 진료 안전성이나 임상 효과로 확대 해석할 수는 없다.

articles.title: MeltKV: Memory-Aligned KV Cache Compression via Variable-Bit Packed Vector Quantization for Long-Context LLMs
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.18652v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly rely on long contexts, making Key-Value (KV) caches dominate memory usage and inference latency. Existing vector quantization (VQ) methods effectively compress KV caches to sub-4-bit levels but often overlook inefficiencies in memory alignment and decoding speed. This work introduces MeltKV, a memory-latency co-optimized KV cache quantization framework for long-context LLM serving. MeltKV employs a memory-aligned variable-bit index packing scheme that adaptively assigns bit-widths to grouped key channels and compactly stores indices within standard data-types, eliminating redundant bits. Additionally, head-wise codebook sharing reduces the total codebook size while maintaining accuracy. Experiments demonstrate that MeltKV effectively compresses KV representations to sub-4-bit levels down to 1 bit and, at comparable perplexity, achieves 48.1% lower memory usage and 52.9% lower latency than state-of-the-art VQ methods.
articles.summary: MeltKV는 긴 문맥 LLM의 KV 캐시를 압축하면서 메모리 사용량과 복원 지연을 함께 최적화하는 벡터 양자화 기법이다. 키 채널 그룹별 가변 비트 인덱스를 표준 자료형에 정렬해 저장하고, 헤드 단위 코드북 공유로 부가 메모리를 줄인다. 연구진은 최저 1비트까지 압축할 수 있으며 유사한 퍼플렉서티 조건에서 기존 선도 벡터 양자화 방식보다 메모리를 48.1%, 지연을 52.9% 줄였다고 보고했다. 긴 문서와 대규모 코드 문맥을 처리하는 서비스의 자원 부담을 낮출 가능성이 있지만, 수치는 논문에서 평가한 조건에 해당한다.

articles.title: D\'ecoupage: Directorial Audio-Visual Control for Long Multi-Shot Video Generation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.18866v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In cinematic storytelling, sound and visual transitions do not always coincide in lockstep: dialogue frequently bridges across cuts to reveal reactions or introduces new scenes via J- and L-cuts, while deliberate silences pace the scene. Existing audio-visual generative frameworks, however, lack explicit mechanisms to coordinate independent visual and acoustic timing over extended horizons. As narrative duration and shot complexity scale, these systems struggle to maintain long-range dialogue pacing, often hallucinating speech during intended silences or erroneously driving mouth movements on silent listeners. To enable fine-grained cinematic control, we present DECOUPAGE, a screenplay-driven framework for long-form, multi-shot, and multi-character joint audio-video generation. Rather than coupling modality boundaries by default, DECOUPAGE uncouples generation into independently bounded visual and acoustic tracks governed by persistent character identities. DECOUPAGE builds on a joint audio-video diffusion model with dual-schedule temporal cross-attention, incorporating a directorial Lip-sync mechanism that selectively decouples speech conditioning from visual facial dynamics during off-screen dialogue. On multi-shot conversational benchmarks, DECOUPAGE achieves precise control over shot transitions, audio timing, and visibility-aware lip synchronization, directing 15- to 60-second screenplay-driven audio-video generation with multimodal coherence.
articles.summary: DECOUPAGE는 대본을 입력받아 여러 인물과 숏으로 구성된 15~60초 길이의 오디오·비디오를 공동 생성하는 프레임워크다. 화면 전환과 음성 구간의 경계를 독립적으로 제어하고 인물 정체성을 유지해, 대사가 컷을 가로지르거나 의도적으로 침묵하는 장면을 표현한다. 공동 확산 모델에 이중 일정 시간 교차 어텐션과 화면 밖 대사를 고려한 립싱크 제어를 적용해, 말하지 않는 인물의 입이 움직이는 문제를 줄이도록 설계됐다. 다중 숏 대화 평가에서 시간 제어와 시청각 일관성을 보고했으며, 정량적인 비교 수치는 제공된 초록에 없다.

articles.title: VideoNexus: Video Perception Beyond the Reasoning Context
articles.content: Understanding long videos requires locating evidence, resolving visual details, and integrating observations into an answer. Even when relevant evidence is present, performing these operations within long, dense visual sequences burdens both perception and reasoning. Video agents enable selective inspection, but returning frames to the planner still accumulates visual information in its reasoning context. Delegating perception reduces this burden, yet sparse sampling can miss decisive details, and per-frame descriptions can preserve context growth. We introduce VideoNexus, a training-free framework that separates detailed video perception from evidence-driven planning and reasoning. The planner controls where to inspect, what to resolve, and how densely to sample. Perception sub-agents process native audio-video in independent contexts and return compact, temporally grounded evidence for iterative search and verification. Using Gemini 3.8 Flash for both planning and perception, VideoNexus achieves 88.6% accuracy on full LVBench, exceeding same-backbone static ingestion and built-in agentic processing by 3.6 and 1.1 points, respectively, at 44% of the latter's measured API cost. A paired LVBench subset ablation shows lower planner input and higher accuracy. With Kimi K3 as the shared backbone, VideoNexus improves over the official Video-GAIA ReAct harness by 8.5 points in our evaluation. These results support compact evidence exchange for combining detailed observation with efficient planning and reasoning.
articles.summary: VideoNexus는 긴 영상의 세부 지각과 계획·추론을 별도 에이전트 문맥으로 분리하는 추가 학습 없는 프레임워크다. 계획 에이전트가 탐색 위치와 샘플링 밀도를 정하면 지각 에이전트가 음성과 영상을 처리하고, 시간 정보가 포함된 간결한 증거만 돌려준다. Gemini 3.8 Flash를 사용한 LVBench 전체 평가에서 정확도 88.6%를 기록해 내장 에이전트 처리보다 1.1%포인트 높았고, 측정 API 비용은 그 방식의 44%였다. 세부 영상 정보를 모두 추론 문맥에 쌓지 않아도 증거 탐색과 검증을 개선할 수 있다는 결과다.

articles.title: Three Invisible Failure Modes in Speech-Based Age Estimation for Child Safety
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.18971v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Child safety in AI depends on the accurate identification of minor users. Young children tend to talk rather than type when interacting with AI, so in practice this identification requires predicting age from speech. We evaluated whether three audio-capable large language models can predict a child's age from their speech across five studies using two speech corpora of children under the age of 13. Models classified children as over 13 on 2.5% to 42.5% of audio responses, and every model that answered placed some 5- to 11-year-olds over 18. While measuring these rates, we uncovered three distinct failure modes. A client library silently double-encoded speech samples, leading one model to classify children aged 5 to 10 years old as being in their thirties and forties with hallucinated explanations. A second model's endpoint was replaced by a successor that refused nearly every age-related question and never produced an age. Every model sometimes placed the same speech sample under 13 and over 18 years of age, but a third model went further, giving threshold answers that contradicted its own numeric estimates. None of these failure modes produced a warning, a status code, or a change in output format, so they would all pass standard monitoring. These results demonstrate why child-safety claims about age assurance should be evaluated at the level of the pipeline rather than the model. We describe the reporting practices that would make such failures detectable.
articles.summary: 음성 지원 LLM 3종을 평가한 연구에서 13세 미만 아동의 발화를 13세 초과로 분류한 비율이 2.5~42.5%에 달했다. 연구진은 음성 이중 인코딩 오류, 후속 모델로의 엔드포인트 교체에 따른 응답 거부, 같은 음성에 대한 연령 판단 불일치라는 세 가지 실패 유형을 확인했다. 이 문제들은 경고·상태 코드·출력 형식 변화 없이 발생해 일반적인 서비스 모니터링으로는 포착하기 어려웠다. 아동 보호용 연령 확인은 모델 정확도뿐 아니라 입력 처리, 모델 변경, 응답 일관성까지 포함한 전체 파이프라인 수준에서 검증해야 한다는 지적이다.

articles.content:
November 16, 2026

How more than 1,800 scientists used ChatGPT—and what they expect AI to mean for scientific discovery. Explore the findings in our new report.

Scientific progress depends on researchers asking new questions and finding ways to answer them. AI is becoming part of that work, but we’re still learning where it helps and what it could mean for discovery.

OpenAI’s Economic Research team studied more than 580,000 scientific messages from 1,819 scientists in the ChatGPT for Academic Researchers summer pilot and surveyed 251 participants.

Scientists used ChatGPT across the research process, from reviewing literature to analyzing evidence and developing ideas. Surveyed participants estimated that the same work, at the same quality, would have taken 1.9 times as long without AI. And 98% of those who answered our question about discovery timelines expected AI to accelerate discovery in their field.

By default, OpenAI does not use participants’ data from the ChatGPT for Academic Researchers program to train its models. To protect researchers’ privacy, we used tools called automated classifiers to sort messages by the type of research activity, such as reviewing literature, writing code, or analyzing data. The research team could see those categories, but did not read the underlying messages or ChatGPT’s responses.

Scientists in this study used ChatGPT to explore ideas, analyze evidence, write code, and communicate their findings. Their responses also point to ambitions beyond saving time: finding more promising questions and pursuing a wider range of research.

Understanding whether those expectations translate into faster discovery will take more research. Progress will also depend on the funding, staff, and experimental capacity scientists need to test their ideas.

articles.title: Policy Optimization With Multiple Verifiers via Pareto Rankings
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.19064v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become an important approach to improving the reasoning capabilities of large language models. In tasks such as code generation and instruction following, multiple verifiers evaluate whether a response satisfies different requirements. Their outcomes provide detailed feedback about partial success, yet this feedback is commonly aggregated into a scalar reward for policy optimization. Rewarding only complete success discards distinctions among partial solutions, while counts and weighted sums impose comparisons between responses that satisfy different subsets of requirements. We introduce Partial-Order Likelihood Policy Optimization (POLPO), which learns from the comparisons established by verification without first constructing an aggregate reward. Pareto dominance identifies responses that satisfy additional requirements without losing any already satisfied, while leaving responses with conflicting outcomes incomparable. POLPO extends the listwise likelihood underlying Direct Preference Optimization by maximizing the total probability of all complete rankings consistent with these partial orders. This objective provides supervision from verified improvements even before complete solutions are available, without requiring a prescribed ordering of incomparable responses. Experiments on code generation and instruction following demonstrate improved learning efficiency and higher rates of complete requirement satisfaction compared with scalar-reward training. These results support partial-order likelihood as an effective approach to learning from multiple verifiers.
articles.summary: POLPO는 코드 생성과 지시 이행에서 여러 검증기의 결과를 단일 보상으로 합산하지 않고, 검증 결과가 만드는 부분 순서를 직접 학습하는 정책 최적화 방법이다. 기존 충족 조건을 잃지 않으면서 추가 조건을 만족한 응답만 파레토 우위로 판단하고, 서로 다른 조건을 충족한 응답 사이에는 임의의 순위를 강제하지 않는다. 이 부분 순서와 일치하는 전체 순위들의 확률을 최대화해 완전한 정답이 나오기 전에도 부분적인 개선에서 학습 신호를 얻는다. 연구진은 스칼라 보상 학습보다 학습 효율과 전체 요구사항 충족률이 높았다고 보고했으며, 복수 조건을 검사하는 코딩·업무 에이전트 훈련에 활용 가능성을 제시했다.
